children: Kalshi has halted offering wagers on whether US President Donald Trump will "mention" specific words on certain dates following an order from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

Kalshi's so-called "mention markets" include contracts that allow traders to wager on whether a specific word or phrase will be said during public events such as speeches, broadcasts or corporate earnings calls
The company's surveillance system had flagged insider trading doubts from these markets to CFTC earlier this year, which included Trump's teleprompter

Such markets have faced regulatory scrutiny, including from the CFTC, over concerns ​that they could be vulnerable to ​insider trading or manipulation by ⁠people with advance access to prepared remarks or speech transcripts

The prediction market platform had already stopped listing a large number of mention markets at the request of the regulator, including all sports event mentions, according to a person familiar with the matter
The markets previously generated a monthly $90 million in trading volume, the person said

A CFTC spokesperson confirmed that the agency had stayed some Kalshi contracts pending further proceedings on their susceptibility to manipulation. This is in keeping with recent CFTC guidance on mention markets, the spokesperson said
The latest development comes at a time when Kalshi is in talks to raise fresh funds at a $65 billion valuation to build a ​new platform for trading compute futures, a source told Reuters last week
